title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Preformed transition-metal complexes of chelating ligands can act as metalloligands to control subsequent lanthanide hydrolysis and give high-nuclearity 3d–4f clusters, whereas earlier Schiff-base metalloligands usually stopped at low nuclearity; the same ligand system can still change composition with pressure and pH.
explanation: Iminodiacetate [M(IDA)] under hydrothermal conditions gave four-shell Gd54Ni54, La60Ni76, and, with mixed ligands, Ni64Ln96. The same IDA chemistry at ambient pressure gave structurally similar Gd52Ni56, in which two Gd(III) and six carbonate ions of Gd54Ni54 are replaced by two Ni(II) and additional hydroxides.
scope: Heterometallic 3d–4f hydroxide clusters assembled with stable chelate metalloligands, especially Ni–IDA, rather than Schiff-base metalloligands.
conditions: Chelating ligand first forms a stable transition-metal complex; hydrolysis then proceeds under hydrothermal or, in the compared case, ambient-pressure conditions.
caveats: Schiff-base versus IDA is a literature contrast cited by the authors, not a head-to-head experiment in one reaction series. Product identity also depends on lanthanide ion and pH.
